machine: Apple M4 Mac mini (base, 16 GB unified)

runtime_settings.source: scripts/start_llama_server.sh defaults; the exact server ctx for these runs was not separately logged (peak observed context was ~16k tokens, well within any setting).

speed.source: estimated from pi transcripts across all gemma sessions (decode = median of per-turn output/dt on generation-heavy turns, n=10, tight 10.2-10.9 cluster; prefill = two clean cold first-turn measurements, both ~142 tok/s, on ~2.0-2.4k-token prompts).
speed.confidence: approximate — decode is well-constrained; prefill rests on few uncached-input points (KV-cache reuse zeroes most turns) and some later turns showed cold-start/idle stalls that were excluded. Run bench_perf.sh against a live server for exact llama-server timings.
speed.comparison_note: Within estimation error this is the SAME speed as qwen3.5-9b-q4_k_m on this machine (prefill ~138, decode ~10.5). The 12B QAT (4-bit) is not meaningfully slower than the 9B Q4 here — both are memory-bandwidth bound on the M4.

exact_benchmark.how: make server MODEL=gemma-4-12b-qat, then: bash evals/bench_perf.sh
